text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Singapore's economy will continue its recovery this year after rebounding from sharp growth slowdown last year, Ministry of Trade and Industry says.
- National Trades Union Congress chief Lim Boon Heng says forthcoming NTUC central committee elections in April will be watershed.
- China shrugs off rumours about deterioration in health of 92-year-old Chinese patriarch Deng Xiaoping, saying condition of elederly statesman remains unchanged.
- Malaysia unveils details of new over-the-counter market for high-tech industries and multi-media companies, saying wholly-owned foreign companies will be allowed to list on new exchange.
- Two new players in market for government industrial land -- Malayan Credit and Pidemco Land -- cast top bids for two parcels.
- Bank of Thailand openly challenges speculators on baht currency, declaring devaluation of baht was "not a policy option to tackle Thailand's current economic problems".
- Indonesia unveils ambitious plans to transform Natuna island, located near one of world's largest natural gas projects, into integrated economic development zone along lines of Batam island.
- Concerns over health of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping rock China and Hong Kong stock markets, with Shenzhen taking the biggest hit.
- Singapore stocks fall as retail investors square positions while institutional investors keep to sidelines ahead of corporate results season.
- Printed circuit board (PCB) manufacturer and SESDAQ aspirant Gul Technologies expanding manufacturing facilities and gearing up to take on more high-end PCB production in next two years.
- Electronics and plastics group Omni Industries raising Singapore $22.9 million from initial public offer of 54 million new shares at 45 Singapore cents each.
